title: Heat Pump Rebates in Oakville 2026: Per-Ton Rebates and What They Cover
desc: Oakville heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings: 78% of households own, and the rebate is $500 per ton for gas or $1,250 for electric, oil, propane and wood.
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Oakville has 73,560 households, 78% of them owners, and 80% live in an eligible house type. Larger houses mean more tons, so the cap matters here.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Oakville
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: The air-source rebate reaches its cap at 6 tons for electric, oil, propane and wood homes ($7,500) and at 4 tons for gas homes ($2,000). A large Oakville house that needs two outdoor units of 3 tons each earns the full $7,500 on electric heat but only $2,000 on gas. Up to three outdoor units count toward the one rebate.

11,005 owner-occupied detached houses were built before 1981, and about 19% of households live in homes built since 2011. 3.3% report needing major repairs. Older houses often need duct changes, and newer ones may already have ductwork sized for a central system.

Ground-source pays $2,000 per ton up to $12,000 for electric, oil, propane and wood homes and a flat $3,000 for gas homes. The system must be a full installation sized for the home's load, with a closed-loop capacity used for the rebate, and direct-expansion systems do not qualify. The program recommends asking the installer to sign a CSA C448 attestation.
A home that already uses a heat pump for space heating is not eligible, and replacing one earns nothing. Ask the program how a cooling-only unit is classified before you apply.

If a large house needs several outdoor units to meet the whole-home requirement, up to three count toward one rebate. The contractor must submit the NRCan sizing form once for each outdoor unit and decide which indoor zones each unit serves. An Oakville owner should ask for the zone map so that the plan is clear before approval.
Payment and what it is for

The rebate is a cheque by mail within 60 days after the post-installation application is approved. It reduces the cost after the fact, so the contract has to be paid first. Ask the contractor whether they offer financing, or consider a loan, and do not assume the cheque will arrive before the final invoice is due.
claim_steps: Estimate the system size in tons and check which fuel category applies.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
